Photo credit should read : Cathal McNaughton/PA <h> How the carbon budget is calculated <p> Each carbon budget represents an emissions ceiling for greenhouse gas , measured in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent . According to the proposed budgets , Ireland can emit 295 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent up to 2025 and then 200 million tonnes from then until the end of the decade . <p> " It 's all done in carbon dioxide equivalent measurements , " said Peter Thorne , member of CCAC and a professor of physical geography at the University of Maynooth . This means the other greenhouse gases such as methane and nitrous oxide are converted into their carbon dioxide equivalent in tonnes to get the emissions limit . <p> " Greenhouse gases have different efficacy . So methane efficacy is 80 times that of carbon dioxide , one molecule of methane has the equivalent greenhouse gases potential to 80 molecules of carbon dioxide , @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ also differ . Carbon dioxide is complex . When that gas is emitted about one third goes into the ocean , another third goes into the terrestrial biosphere and the rest " hangs around for a very long time . " <p> Comparatively , methane emissions have a much shorter lifespan . <p> " If I put a tonne of methane into the atmosphere today , in 12 years time half of that tonne will remain and in 24 years time the quarter will remain so within a century effectively all of that methane will have disappeared , " Thorne said . <h> How do they know how much greenhouse gases are being released <p> Calculating how many emissions are arising from what activity can be relatively easy or difficult depending on what you are looking at , according to Thorne . <p> Emissions arising from fossil fuels are relatively simply to calculate . " We know how efficiently that fossil fuel is burned , we know the volume of that fossil fuel and its weight , we know how much carbon is in there , " Thorne said . @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ the emissions for an individual cow , taking a representative sample and then doing a headcount of the number of cattle and their lifetimes to give a reasonable estimate of their emissions . <p> Land use , land use change and forestry are very difficult to measure . Areas where the land has been drained or a denuded peat bog are particularly difficult to calculate . With land you also have the issue that over a given area some of it may be a carbon source ( it emits carbon dioxide ) and other areas a carbon sink ( it absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere ) . <p> " So some of the numbers of our emissions are very well known , highly certain . @@63484318 <h> Hungry polar bears forced to seek food in human settlements <p> We 've all heard the polar ice caps are melting . Experts have been saying it for years . In Novaya Zemlya , a small cluster of islands in northern Russia , hungry polar bears have been searching for food in human settlements . <h> What 's happening ? <p> Polar bears , who usually feed on fatty seals , can eat up to 100 lbs of blubber in one sitting . However , the loss of ice in the Arctic has made it difficult ( if not impossible ) for them to get access to seals , who spend most of their time in the water . In the Novaya Zemlya area of Russia , the bears have been left stranded on land . <p> While the polar bears may benefit from eating alternative foods ( such as stray animals or items found in human refuse ) , Polar Bears International says there is no evidence these food @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , to sustain the polar bears ' population level . <p> We 're not just talking about one rogue bear who strayed off-path , either . With the ice melting so rapidly , the bears are being forced ashore . " Some polar bears may suffer from malnutrition , and in extreme cases -- especially females with cubs -- they may face starvation , " says the WWF.

@@63488955 <h> What you need to know ahead of the world 's biggest climate conference this weekend <p> Participants seen holding a banner at the protest . Ahead of Glasgow Climate Summit COP26 , a large coalition of activists and community leaders rallied across the country demanding a strong stand against climate change . In New York City , activists with Rainforest Action Network unfurled a giant CODE RED ! banner in front of the United Nations headquarters . ( Photo by Erik McGregor/Sipa USA ) <p> Stay on top of the latest issues at home and abroad by signing up to our FREE daily newsletter <p> Invalid EmailSomething went wrong , please try again later . <p> We use your sign-up to provide content in ways you 've consented to and to improve our understanding of you . This may include adverts from us and 3rd parties based on our understanding . You can unsubscribe at any time.More info <p> The 26th Conference of the Parties is about to begin . The United Nations Climate Change Conference , better known as COP26 will take place from Sunday , 31 October to 12 November . <p> The two-week conference provides @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ a global level and on a global stage . The annual conferences gather all nations that have signed the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change ( UNFCCC ) . All 193 UN member states have signed the UNFCCC as well as Palestine , the Cook Islands and Niue . The Vatican is an observer to the treaty . <h> COP26 is highly anticipated <p> For this COP , the UK and Italy are joint hosts and the conference will take place in Glasgow . About 25,000 people are expected to attend . This year 's conference is set to be particularly important . The UK has already called on countries to increase their emissions reduction targets so that the world can be at net-zero carbon emissions by 2050 . With current targets , the world is on track to be 2.7C warmer on average than pre-industrial levels by the end of this century , according to the United Nations . <p> Many of the issues that have been unresolved since the landmark Paris Agreement in 2015 are hoped to be settled at this international summit . The most important @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ . <p> Activists are seen next to a banner , calling on the government to invest in a plant-based future at COP26 ( climate change conference ) , on the Home Office building during the demonstration . Animal Rebellion activists scaled the Home Office building in Westminster , which includes the Department For Environment , Food and Rural Affairs ( Defra ) , calling on the UK government to stop subsidising the meat industry and to invest in a plant-based future . ( Photo by Vuk Valcic / SOPA Images/Sipa USA ) <h> The goal is 1.5C warming <p> The US presidential special envoy on climate change has called COP26 " the last best chance the world has " to act on the environment . The world badly needs to reduce the amount of greenhouse gas emissions ( mostly carbon dioxide and methane ) if we are to keep the world to 1.5C of warming and no more . <p> The latest report from The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change ( IPCC ) said it was inevitable that the world would reach 1.5C in the next 20 years , and @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ was needed to reduce emissions to prevent the global average temperature increasing to 2C , at which point the impacts of climate change would be catastrophic . We are currently at around 1.1C warmer than pre-industrial times . <p> 1.5C is not seen by the IPCC as a safe level , but their reports have shown that anything beyond it will have serious consequences . All announced pledges will not get us to a 1.5C world , the warmer it gets , the worse it is for the planet . COP26 has been called on to catalyse the actions required to get the world to 1.5C warmed and no more . <h> What else is on the COP26 agenda ? <p> Everyone who comes to COP will have their own agenda but a key consideration is the disparity between higher-income countries that are responsible for more emissions and lower-income countries that are experiencing more harms and threats of harm due to climate change . <p> Currently the United States and China account for almost half of all global greenhouse gas emissions . Not a single developed nation is deemed to @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ warming . <p> Financing will also be a huge issue at COP26 . Since 2009 , developed countries have promised to give $100 billion ( ? 86 billion ) per year to help the countries most vulnerable to the impact of climate change transition to clean energy and more climate change resilient infrastructure . Of the 23 developed countries responsible for providing international climate finance , most have not been paying their fair share of the annual $100 billion . <p> Carbon trading ( a system that allows countries and companies who fail to meet their emission-reduction targets to buy allowances from others that come under their budget ) will also be on the agenda . Other issues will include how to adapt to climate change in terms of infrastructure , utilities , food production and warning systems . <p> A little girl looks at her grandpa playing a song in support of the Climate Miles walkers waiting outside of the station . In the run-up to the United Nations COP26 climate conference that will take place in Glasgow , hundreds of climate activists are walking from the North of @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ action needed to keep the earth livable for future generations . Led by Marjan Minnesma , a Dutch environmental activist and director of the Urgenda Foundation , the activists departed from the Rotterdam train station to Scotland . At the station , climate activists from several groups were there to see them off at departure . ( Photo by Ana Fernandez / SOPA Images/Sipa USA ) <h> Who will be at COP26 <p> All countries that have signed up to UNFCCC will send delegates to COP26 . The leaders of many countries as well as relevant ministers will be there . Of the top five polluting countries : China , US , India , Russia and Japan respectively , the leaders of two , China and Russia , will not attend COP26 . This is seen as a huge blow for international cooperation on meeting the 1.5C goal . India 's prime minister will attend after some wavering . <p> As well as nations , hundreds of non-governmental organisations have a standing invitation to attend as observers to COP26 . The Irish Independent reports that 520 organisations sought permission to @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ <p> Activist Greta Thunberg will be there , but she is n't expecting much , according to The Guardian . Extinction Rebellion is also planning to protest outside COP26 to demand faster action on climate change from world leaders , the BBC reports . <p> Also attending are a Global Citizen 's Assembly of 100 people from around the world who will present their findings at the international conference . The Guardian reports that the members will be chosen via lottery but will be a representative sample of Earth 's people .

A bowel disease ? Me ? Why me ? -- these were the constant questions I asked myself every day for three months straight . It 's hard to come to terms with something so life-changing , and not for the better . <p> I suffer from Crohn 's disease , a chronic Inflammatory Bowel Disease ( IBD ) . I was diagnosed just over seven months ago , one month before my 23rd birthday . I was having the time of my life on my year J1 visa in New York City , when suddenly I had to cancel my internship and visa and come home straight away , as my insurance did n't cover the treatment I needed in the States . <p> When I was diagnosed in May last year , every day was a struggle , especially since I was sick for the whole summer . I lost so much weight in New York between sitting in my apartment in Queens unable to move , eat or drink for two weeks straight . I was completely malnourished from constantly vomiting and going to the toilet , I was as white as a ghost and severely anaemic . I suffered from bad cramps and loose stool movements , and not the usual stomach cramps , it felt like someone was trying to tear out my insides . On top of that , I was constantly bloated , suffered from bad mouth ulcers , mood swings , hot and cold chills , weight loss , and the dreaded haemorrhoids . It was only in the last year that I started noticing a lot of blood in my stools ( lovely I know ) . My whole body was in pain , from my joints to my muscles , and to my mental state . This led to me becoming quite depressed and anxious , making matters a whole lot worse . <p> I was taking several different medications at a time for over four months , but the worst of them all was the steroid called prednisone ( anyone who has been on these can sympathise with me ) . These are truly the worst steroids in the world , I gained so much weight , I suffered from moon face , which made me look like a chipmunk ( and not a cute one ) . I started receiving Infliximab ( Remicade ) infusions every 2 months , which is an auto-immune suppressant drug used to treat IBD . This was all going on while my friends were out enjoying their summer , it was the worst few months of my life ! I also dealt with a bad infection ( C-diff ) that really affected my treatment , which set back my road to remission . <p> A lot of my friends did n't really understand exactly what Crohn 's was at first , same with my family and of course , I do n't blame them , I barely knew what it was . To be honest , I still do n't think they really understand how it affects me both physically and mentally , I mean how can they ? Cancelling plans last minute is n't because I do n't want to see you or spend time with you , it 's because I genuinely feel like crap . My friends are off to the UK in February for a girly , booze-filled trip . As much as I would love to go , I know that my body would just crash and burn . The symptoms come and go , but mostly I do suffer with them , whether it 's pain , fatigue , constant bowel movements , or just not feeling happy and sociable in general . <p> Cancelling plans last minute is n't because I do n't want to see you or spend time with you , it 's because I genuinely feel like crap . <p> I do n't " have " to avoid certain foods , but I do and anyone with this disease will know what I mean by that . If I want to avoid pain and horrible symptoms then yes , I do " have " to avoid certain foods . For me , vegetables high in fibre seem to make things worse . A lot of the time it 's really mind over matter . Stress is a major factor and trigger for flare-ups , if I was to stress about what to eat and what not to eat every day , then I would probably be in a rut . Sometimes you have to treat yourself or simply include the types of foods that cause symptoms , I believe it builds up the strength of my body and digestive system . It 's funny how eating certain foods for me is a risk , but I 'm willing to take them so that I can gain control over my body . <p> I also get a lot of people telling me how AMAZING and HEALTHY I look , and yes that 's a nice thing to hear , but it 's not necessarily the case . Some days I 'll be sat at my desk at work in excruciating pain , hunched over , goosebumps and shakes going through my body and I look fine , absolutely fine . No change in colour , no redness , just the pain that hides inside my body . A lot of people do n't really understand exactly what IBD is , and I 'm not one bit surprised . The publicity and acknowledgement of Ulcerative Colitis and Crohn 's disease in Ireland is shocking . No one knows how it 's caused , the right treatments to use , yet more than 40,000 people suffer from this chronic and life term illness ! Something needs to be done , and that 's why last year I decided to volunteer for the ISCC ( Irish Society For Colitis And Crohn 's Disease ) to spread awareness . <p> When someone asks me what triggers the disease , I 'm not exactly sure how to answer . I have been dealing with anxiety for a few years so maybe that 's a factor ? When I was in New York before I got diagnosed , I was working six , sometimes seven days a week , on top of partying . I was torturing my body , so I can only imagine what that did to my overall health and wellbeing . In my opinion , genetics is definitely a major factor for me , my cousin has Crohn 's , my uncle suffers from psoriasis and my granddad had rheumatoid arthritis , all auto-immune diseases too . <p> The publicity and acknowledegment of Ulcerative Colitis and Crohn 's disease in Ireland is shocking . No one knows how it 's caused , the right treatments to use , yet more than 40,000 people suffer from this chronic and life term illness ! <p> This disease has changed my life in many ways , but the one positive thing I 'll say about it all is that I have become a much stronger person because of it . I appreciate the small things in life , and even though I still have my bad days , this all could have been a whole lot worse . I try to live each day as a brand new day and remain positive . Hopefully that will get me through life a happy and ( somewhat ) healthy woman .

@@63494370 <h> Climate needs less talk , more action <p> ' Cop ' stands for Conference of the Parties . It 's called Cop26 because it is the 26th such event and will be attended by the countries that signed the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change ( UNFCCC ) , in 1994 . <p> There was no summit last year , due to Covid , and this year 's event runs from October 31st until November 12th , hosted by the UK and Italy . It is appropriate that it kicks off on Hallowe'en night , because the world is certainly in a scary place right now . <p> Every year brings more broken records , for heat , for floods , for forest fires , for melting ice , and the extinction of various species of wildlife . <p> The speed at which Planet Earth is changing is speeding up in itself . Every prediction for temperature changes , for the greening of the ice caps , for rising oceans , has had to be revised upwards in recent years . <p> This year 's summit is , without doubt , the most important yet . <p> @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ are bringing forward their own measures for dealing with the crisis , and just days after our own carbon budgets were published here in Ireland . <p> This is the first time that Ireland has set limits on greenhouse gas emissions for set periods of time . <p> The budgets , announced earlier this week , are part of a roadmap of actions that are set out in the Climate Action Act , which was signed into law in July . The Act commits Ireland to reach a legally-binding target of net-zero emissions no later than 2050 , and a cut of 51% by 2030 , compared to 2018 levels . <p> This week Minister Eamon Ryan hinted that the ' journey ' to ' net zero ' , which commits us to the transition to a ' climate resilient , biodiversity rich , environmentally sustainable and climate neutral economy ' wo n't be easy . <p> ' Every sector of the economy will need to play its part , ' he said . ' There will be different targets for each sector , based on their respective starting points @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ of reducing emissions . ' <p> There is no doubt that certain sectors of the economy are feeling more put-upon than others by these commitments . The farming sector , the motor industry , transport in general and fuel suppliers all feel they are having fingers pointed at them , but the real truth is that every one of us will be asked to step up to the mark . <p> As this weekend 's conference will no doubt hear , the time for talking is long over . Greta Thunberg 's speech earlier this year at the Youth4Climate summit , dubbed the ' blah , blah , blah ' speech -- in which she mocked the world 's governments and big corporates -- summed up what many of us were thinking . <p> There have been many empty platitudes expressed in recent years about ' carbon zero ' and lowering emissions -- but now it 's time for action . If we allow the noise generated by certain sectors to drown out the urgency of the situation we are facing , the record-breaking data on temperature and Armageddon-type disasters @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ fears , now , that Australia 's arrogance will garner support from other nations who are already reluctant to pursue a low emissions strategy . But such dangerous moves are not just a threat to the planet , but to the future of humanity itself . <p> As Theodore Roosevelt said : ' Nothing in the world is worth having or worth doing unless it means effort , pain , difficulty . ' <p> Ironically , if we do n't act now , and take on board that effort , pain and difficulty , we wo n't have any world to worry about .

This may include adverts from us and 3rd parties based on our understanding . You can unsubscribe at any time.More info <p> US plastics are on course to take over from coal in terms of greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 . According to a report from Bennington College 's Beyond Plastics project , the plastics industry in the US will be more polluting than the country 's coal industry by the end of the decade . <h> Plastic pollution <p> The report found that the American plastics industry is releasing at least 232 million tonnes of greenhouse gases annually , the equivalent to 116 average-sized coal-fired power plants . <p> Nationwide , the US plastics industry reported it released 114 million tonnes of greenhouse gases in 2020 , however the spread is very disproportionate . Of its reported climate change pollution , 90 per cent occurs @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ less than the US average , with 67 per cent more likely to be minority communities . <p> Plastic pollution and climate change are twin issues . The report identified 10 different stages in which the manufacture of plastics emits the most significant greenhouse gases . <p> For example , hydro-fracking is expected to release 45 million tonnes of methane annually in the US by 2025 . Transporting and processing fracked gases emits roughly 4.8 million tonnes of methane each year . <p> The exporting and importing of plastic 's raw materials and products emits at least 51 million tonnes of greenhouse gases annually . <p> Since 2019 , at least 42 US plastics facilities have opened , are under construction or are in the permitting process . If the facilities become fully operational , they could release an additional 55 million tonnes of greenhouse gases , the equivalent of a further 27 500-megawatt coal-fired power plants by 2025 . <h> Plastics and global warming <p> " The scale of the plastics industry 's greenhouse gas emissions is staggering , but it 's equally concerning that few people in government @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , " Judith Enck , president of Beyond Plastics , told Reuters . <p> However , 232 million tonnes of greenhouse gases a year emitted by the plastics industry is likely an underestimate . The report said that they have likely undercounted emissions and air pollution related to different stages of the production of plastics and export of plastic waste . <p> US regulations do not require the plastic industry to report their emissions and no federal agency tracks them .

@@63494544 <h> Older people -- Left behind <p> Mohammed Hassan Khan <p> 30 October , 2021 , 4:11 pm <p> Residents , board members and guests during the World Elder Abuse day . Picture : SOPHIE RALULU/FILE <p> As Fiji and the Pacific Island nations have started gearing up for the cyclone season , it is the right time to call for the inclusion of the older persons in national and district disaster preparedness of Government and civil society organisations . <p> Having spent several years working in humanitarian crises it was not so surprising to me that older people often get overlooked in the response . <p> Perhaps this the reason for the older persons to choose to stay in their own homes and village surroundings . <p> The fact that most of the older persons died at home during the COVID-19 crisis is strong testimony for care of the elders in family and in their own communities . <p> With limited resources and the imperative to save lives , aid agencies rightly focus much of their efforts on those most visibly in need , such as children and women . <p> However , with the changing population dynamics @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ <p> It is also important for major civil society organisations to set programs for the older persons . <p> The humanitarian principle of humanity , however , means that everyone should be treated equally , while the principle of impartiality requires assistance to be targeted where it is needed most , regardless of age . <p> In this regard the COVID-19 pandemic has put into sharp focus how older people can be disproportionately impacted by crises . <p> They faced the highest risk of death from the virus and significant secondary impacts . <p> However , it is not only in public health emergencies that older people are suffering . They are often hardest hit in environmental disasters and armed conflicts . <p> The international community is failing in its commitments to protect the rights of older people in emergencies , as a new report by Age International and Help Age International -- If not now , when ? -- shows . <p> It is high time action is taken to prioritise older people in humanitarian action to provide the assistance that they clearly need and deserve . <p> The @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ not the priority at any level of disasters and most recently the COVID-19 pandemic . <p> Urgent action is required to correct this situation . <p> The outcome report of nationwide consultations with older persons , conducted by the National Council on Older Persons ( NCOP ) late last year was explicit in its call for the inclusion of older persons and that they are not left behind and that there was an urgent need to re-assess the facilities at the various of the evacuation centres . <p> The participants were particularly concerned about the unfriendly nature of toilet and ablution facilities for the elderly . <p> The specific needs of older people <p> The HelpAge International report provides the broadest-ever survey of the situation of older people affected by humanitarian crises , drawing on needs assessments conducted in 11 countries , over a 13-month period . <p> It paints a bleak picture about how older people 's needs are not being met . Of the 8883 people assessed : 20 per cent had no shelter , 64 per cent did not have enough to eat , 77 per cent @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ health services , and 25 per cent had no access to drinking water . <p> Older people are far more likely to live with a disability ( 40 per cent of those assessed ) , but rarely are provided with assistive devices . <p> The mental health burden of crisis is particularly acute for older people who face neglect and isolation : a quarter of those assessed said they could not cope ( more so for women than men ) . <p> Neglected and discriminated against <p> The HAI report makes two other important points : One , it says " worse still , older people suffer doubly in crises : not only are they disproportionately impacted , but they are also neglected and discriminated in the response " . <p> Two ; A lack of age-disaggregated data renders them invisible in most humanitarian plans while one-size-fits-all programs fail to consider their specific needs . 77 per cent of older people assessed said they had not been consulted by humanitarian agencies . Two in five older people said they could not reach aid distribution points independently , often needing the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ the help of NCOP must do a similar exercise on the facilities in Fiji as evacuation centres are not elderly friendly . <p> Misconceptions about older people <p> In Fiji our cultural and religious norms have emphasized tolerance and patience which is contributing to the widespread misconceptions about the experience of older people in emergencies , which is contributing to their lack of prioritisation . <p> While it might be expected that older people receive support from family members , there is marked increase in those who live alone . Ironically , when they do live with family members , they are more likely to be the carer rather than being the one cared for , as it well known that role grandparents in caring for children is a cultural fact for Fiji . <p> Older people are often considered economically inactive and yet they can provide an important contribution to household incomes in many ways . <p> Time for action <p> While aid agencies have taken action to prioritise the needs of other vulnerable groups , such as women , children and persons with disabilities , older people continue @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ the Sustainable Development Goals ( SDGs ) with the commitment to " leave no one behind " , but this is precisely what is happening for older people . <p> In Fiji a new approach is long overdue , but will only come about through strong humanitarian leadership and robust action . The UN secretary-general published a welcome policy note on the impact of COVID-19 on older people early this year . This now needs to be translated into a system-wide strategy to address the gaps in the UN response that COVID-19 has exposed . <p> Humanitarian appeals should be based on age-disaggregated data and outline the specifi c needs of older people , with humanitarian programs designed to address these needs prioritised in funding decisions . Relevant guidelines and standards exist , but they need to be implemented . <p> There is an emerging agenda to promote more inclusive humanitarian action and older people must be at the centre of this . The humanitarian system is facing unprecedented challenges , but it would be unjust to neglect the rights of older people . <p> As the global and Fiji @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ crises , like the COVID-19 pandemic , climate change issues and the usual natural disaster , will grow rapidly making this an unavoidable issue that humanitarians can no longer avoid and must prioritise instead . <p> There is no room for complacency in this matter . <p> MOHAMMED HASSAN KHAN is a convenor with Fiji Pacific Network For The Right Of The Older Persons ( Fpnrop ) . @@63494754 <p> In October 2020 , NHS England and NHS Improvement ( NHSE&amp;I ) approved an ambitious new strategy to become the world 's first national health service to agree net zero emissions commitments as part of the global effort to tackle climate change . <p> To hold itself accountable , it set two main targets : to become net zero by the year 2040 for emissions it controls directly , referred to as the NHS Carbon Footprint , and to achieve net zero by 2045 for emissions it influences but does not directly control , referred to as the NHS Carbon Footprint Plus . <p> Of all the emissions generated by the NHS , medicines account for 25% , and there is a significant focus on two groups -- anaesthetic gases ( 2% of emissions ) and inhalers ( 3% of emissions ) -- where emissions occur at the ' point of use ' ? 1 ? . <p> Efforts to reduce emissions from anaesthetic gases are already taking effect . 2 ? . <p> But it is one specific PCN incentive , adopted in October 2021 , that has generated heated debate among respiratory specialists , which encourages switching patients from metered-dose inhalers ( MDIs ) to dry powder inhalers ( DPIs ) and soft mist inhalers ( SMIs ) . <p> " Our aim is that , in line with best practice in other European countries , by 2023/2024 , only 25% of non-salbutamol inhalers prescribed will be MDI inhalers , @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ is that , in general , DPIs and SMIs offer a low-carbon alternative to MDIs . <p> Dry powder inhalers are n't as green as we think they are <p> Garry McDonald , respiratory pharmacist consultant <p> But respiratory experts argue that , when considering the whole life cycle of the inhaler and the use of inhalers by patients , this is not always the case . <p> " The ' NHS long term plan ' simply stated switching to a lower carbon inhaler to deliver a 4% reduction in the carbon footprint of health and social care , " explains Garry McDonald , a respiratory pharmacist consultant who works across the UK , " but that message has been diluted and misheard to mean that it has to be a DPI ; dry powders are n't as green as we think they are . To replace them , pharmaceutical companies developed CFC-free MDIs , containing hydrofluroalkane ( HFA ) propellants . <p> However , this did not solve all of the environmental problems associated with these devices ; there is now increasing attention on the environmental impacts of HFAs , which are themselves powerful greenhouse gases ? 4 ? . <p> " Most inhalers use HFA134 as a propellant , which has a high global warming impact , and a small number use HFA227 , which has a very high global warming impact , " explains Capstick . <p> DPIs do not require a propellant , which is why they are favoured as a low-carbon option ; instead , they rely on the patient breathing in quickly to inhale the drug into their lungs .
